newsitem.title: CANADA: Forex traders meeting may stabilize Canada dollar.
newsitem.headline: Forex traders meeting may stabilize Canada dollar.

text.p: A conference of the world's top currency traders in Toronto starting on Thursday could limit volatility in the Canadian dollar ahead of the Canadian election next Monday.

The 39th annual meeting of the Association Cambiste International (ACI) comes just days before the June 2 vote and with the Canadian currency under pressure from polls showing the governing Liberals facing a smaller parliamentary majority or even a minority government.

"One would expect the market to be a little bit volatile given that the race seems to be a lot closer than it had been discounted at the beginning of the campaign," said Andrew Spence, senior economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Canada Ltd.
While the foreign exchange dealers are in town to hear speeches by influential politicians, economists and bankers, they are also expected to explore the risks to their Canadian dollar investments.

Royal Bank of Canada foreign exchange director and ACI's Canadian chapter president, Robert Wittmann, told Reuters that the presence of so many top dealers in Canada would likely limit the currency volatility tied to election uncertainty.

"We have over 60 countries represented and over 50 exhibitors," said Wittmann. "I think holding the congress virtually congruent with an election could be seen as fortuitous in as much that you have a lot of senior representatives of the global foreign exchange community very close to people who consider themselves to be specialists in the Canadian dollar."

A Reuters daily tracking poll on Wednesday conducted by Zogby International showed support for Prime Minister Jean Chretien's Liberals falling to 39.7 percent -- below the key 40 percent level for the first time.
"If the tracking poll trends continue, Chretien may not win a majority," said pollster John Zogby.
The Canadian dollar hit its weakest levels in two weeks on Tuesday after falling almost one Canadian cent against the U.S. dollar to C$1.3852 ($0.7219).
Canada's dollar ended flat on Wednesday at 1.3824 ($0.7233) from the morning's open.
The ACI has about 25,000 members in about 60 countries and is meeting in Toronto for the first time since its initial Canadian conference in 1985.

The conference speakers include Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen, New York Federal Reserve Bank President William McDonough, Bundesbank council member Wendelin Hartmann, South African Reserve Bank Governor Christopher Stals and Chilean Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat.
